name: Setaria

project_scope.caution: Not a complete Setaria checklist; S. italica is CULTIVATED/INTRODUCED. Uninstalled S. pumila and S. viridis are comparison aids, not counted canonical cards. Nativity statuses not reaudited.

look_here_first: SETARIA: Foxtails have persistent BRISTLES (sterile branchlets) beneath flower spikelets, NOT true awns. View an intact spikelet and count its own bristles. Compare FOUR canonical examples: introduced annual S. italica has a very dense often heavy head, generally 1–3 bristles; native S. parviflora has short hard knotty RHIZOMES and 4–12 bristles; S. reverchonii is slender interrupted with very sparse bristles typically 2–8 mm WHERE PRESENT; S. scheelei has long conspicuous projecting, generally solitary bristles ~10–35 mm. Do not infer bristle counts, rooting status or nativity from an overview picture.

priority: Find attached spikelet and its persistent bristles; never mistake florets' awns/stigmas for basal sterile branches
Count 1–3 versus 4–12 bristles attached to multiple mature spikelets using 10–20×
Measure long projecting scheelei bristle 10–35 mm against reverchonii 2–8 mm where bristles occur
Compare crowded heavy millet head, short uniform parviflora head, interrupted reverchonii head and long tapered scheelei head
Verify annual fibrous millet vs perennial knotty parviflora/reverchonii on legal rooted specimen

recognition.safety: Don't disturb protected sites or parks to expose rhizomes. Photograph an allowable rooted specimen or leave duration uncertain.

comparison_lesson.title: Setaria — bristles are NOT awns
comparison_lesson.memory_rule: ITALICA introduced annual heavy head & 1–3 BRISTLES; PARVIFLORA rhizomes & 4–12; REVERCHONII interrupted sparse 2–8mm; SCHEELEI long usually single 10–35mm
quick_split: FOXTAIL MILLET (INTRODUCED annual crop/escape): start with stout annual culms, broad foliage, and a heavy dense often lobed or nodding foxtail head. Flora of North America usually describes 1–3 persistent subtending bristles (to ~12 mm), NOT 'numerous bristles beneath every spikelet'. A crop-derived head varies greatly; distinguish from perennial native bristlegrasses using rooted duration, panicle shape and ripe spikelets.

KNOTROOT BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): FIRST verify a living short hard knotty basal rhizome, then a generally short even-width dense foxtail head (~3–8 cm). FNA reports 4–12 persistent bristles, 2–12 mm long, beneath each spikelet; they must be counted from a genuinely intact head at 10–20×. Our only stored macro shows green bracts and pink emergent floral tissue with a 2-mm scale, NOT the perennial rhizome or a countable group of 4–12 basal bristles.

REVERCHON'S BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): the existing real photo shows a skinny, often interrupted upright flowering head, with widely separated spikelet groupings. Its bristles are sparse—some spikelets appear almost unbristled—but FNA gives bristles about 2–8 mm where present; do NOT teach a hard ≤2 mm cutoff. Seek short knotty rhizomes, the stiff hair ligule (1–2 mm), and mature 2.1–4.5 mm spikelets. No bristle measurement is visible in the original picture.

SOUTHWESTERN / SCHEELE'S BRISTLEGRASS (perennial): a tall, commonly broad-leaved and hairy grass with a long, tapered, rather open bottlebrush-like head. Usually 1 (sometimes 2–3) LONG separate projecting bristles per spikelet, typically 10–35 mm in FNA/Kew. Unlike Reverchon's shorter sparse bristles, these long bristles are actually obvious in the saved flowering photograph. Edwards Plateau shady limestone canyon habitat is supportive, not conclusive.
guardrails: Current physical Setaria photos establish large-scale plant architecture only: they do not demonstrate the scientific bristle counts or exact lengths until matched ruler macros are acquired.
The source photo for S. parviflora has protruding pink flower tissue and a 2-mm scale; never mistake its pink plume for multiple persistent subtending bristles.
FNA reports S. italica 1–3 bristles to ~12 mm (original 'numerous' teaching corrected).
FNA reports S. reverchonii bristles 2–8 mm, although often absent on some flowering branches; remove misleading hard ≤2-mm cutoff.
S. scheelei solitary or occasionally more long bristles, not just the silhouette of any densely seeded millet.
S. pumila and S. viridis are uninstalled look-alikes, NOT additional canonical taxa; species-level county native classifications remain unchanged.

comparison_matrix.title: Four Setaria — count bristles ON the spikelet, then check head and rootstock
rows: Dense crop head often 8–30 cm, sometimes lobed or drooping
Short, dense and even cylinder ~3–8(10) cm
Long tapered moderately open ~15–35 cm in Texas sources
Sparse or absent on some branches; where present ~2–8 mm (FNA)
Short knotty rhizomes; hair-fringe ligule <1 mm (FNA)
Short sometimes knotty rhizomes; stiff hair ligule ~1–2 mm
Perennial base; broad blade; ligule ~1–2 mm
Dense curved heads and relatively broad leaves
Green bract-like parts, pink flower tuft, photographer's 2-mm scale; NOT 4–12 count
Thin interrupted axis with separated spikelet clusters; NOT exact short bristles
Tapered green head, distinct large projecting bristles; NOT one-to-one bristle attachment

what_to_teach_crew: Find a true spikelet, then tell the persistent hairy sterile branch BRISTLE from floret awns or purple exserted flower structures.
Photograph two to five mature attachments and COUNT bristles; then actually measure with mm scale, not guessed from head photo.
A thick milletlike crop head is NOT a stand-alone introduced ID. Confirm cultivated annual rootstock and true spikelets.
Only S. parviflora has the characteristic short HARD KNOTTY rhizomes paired with MANY (4–12) bristles here; do not dig without authorization.
S. reverchonii can look almost bristleless; FNA 2–8 mm when present, versus conspicuous long 10–35 mm bristles of Scheele's.
See actual photo arrows for panicle form and long Scheele bristles. The parviflora macro shows a pink flowering tuft that must not be falsely called a bristle.
Check true leaf ligule, mature glumes and fully rooted base when practical; otherwise use provisional Setaria sp.

visual_comparison.title: Setaria — photographed foxtail bristle anatomy, ligules and true perennial rhizomes
visual_comparison.subtitle: Four local canonical Setaria members. Exact source-backed S. parviflora underground stems and 3-mm measured floral parts added alongside original 4-species photo comparisons. Source origin Croatia; no local voucher claimed.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: In Setaria look at individual SPIKELET BRISTLES (sterile accessory branches), not purple STIGMAS. Then check perennial knotty RHIZOME, true LIGULE and glumes/lemmas. Different species may share similar foxtail heads.
